text:
Isha: Heads up — around 09:12 UTC we started seeing a spike in GPU attach failures in us-central1, provisioning stalled for ~20m. infra-bot posted alarms.
infra-bot: [09:12] attach_fail_rate=7.2% pool=gpu-prod-usc1 affected_hosts=host-23..host-34
Ryan: Logs? stack traces?
Jordan: Quick dump shows repeated write-after-sync discrepancies from SMART on a subset of local drives (same vendor lot). Not full drive death, looks like partial writes to certain sectors.
Jordan: snippet: ```smartctl -a /dev/nvme0n1 | egrep "Model|Serial|Firmware|Error Count|Media Errors"
Model Number: ACME NVMe X123
Serial Number: ACME-LOT-A-000123
Firmware Version: 3.4.1-rc2
Media and Data Integrity Errors: 12
```
Maya: Those firmware versions match the recent roll from last week (3.4.1-rc2). Can we isolate hosts with that firmware?
Isha: Isolation yes, but draining 12 hosts drops capacity by ~18%. Need fallback to keep SLAs.
Ryan: Short-term: route new small jobs to preemptible pool and throttle janitor/compactor to avoid heavy writeback on affected hosts. Ops can migrate critical GPU workloads off tagged hosts.
Jordan: We're also seeing EIOs on writeback for some extents — not full filesystem corruption, more like unreadable partial extents after flush. Kernel logs: ```kernel: writeback: EIO on sector 0x1f4a3a - after sync```
Maya: Proposal: tag hosts with fw-batch-A, pause aggressive cleaners on them, and add a read-after-write verification to healthcheck to detect these partial-write failures automatically.
Isha: Agree. Action plan: (1) Tag affected hosts fw-batch-A (2) Pause janitor/compaction on tagged hosts (3) Migrate GPUs off tagged hosts (4) Add read-after-write healthcheck rule (5) Create vendor RMA with serials. I'll own 1-3.
Ryan: Commands I'm running to tag + pause scrub on host-23..host-34: ```rbctl host tag add host-23 fw-batch-A; rbctl host set-attr host-23 scrub.pause=true; rbctl host drain host-23 --reason "fw-batch-A partial-write risk"```
ops-bot: Started migration of 12 VMs from host-23..host-34, strategy=live-migrate prioritise=GPU-critical ETA=35m
Jordan: I pushed a quick dd-based verify script to run on newly-written blocks to detect mismatch: ```for d in /dev/nvme*n1; do dd if=/dev/zero of=$d bs=4M count=16 conv=fdatasync; dd if=$d bs=4M count=16 | cmp - /dev/zero || echo "mismatch on $d"; done``` Run with caution on non-production or after marking the host drained.
Maya: I'll prepare a canary healthcheck PR to add read-after-write checks and a quarantine rule: if mismatch_rate > 2% over 10m then auto-quarantine host.
Ryan: Opening vendor RMA now, attaching SMART logs + firmware + serials. Cost note: re-routing steady state to preemptible pool will add ~\"$4k/day\" if this persists for >24h. Logging cost owner: @finance.
Jordan: Important risk note: continuing heavy janitor compactions on these drives may increase partial-write incidence. Recommend immediate pause until we confirm.
Maya: :thumbsup: starting pause and canary rollout. I'll report back after the first 10m window.
ops-bot: migration progress: 8/12 VMs completed, 4 in progress (ETA 18m)
Isha: Update +45m: attach error rate in gpu-prod-usc1 down from 7.2% -> 0.9% after tagging + migration + janitor pause. Still monitoring for read-after-write mismatches. Leaving thread open for root-cause and RMA updates.
Ryan: Once vendor confirms, we should decide: rollback FW to 3.4.0 or accelerate replacement RMA. If rollback, schedule maintenance window — rollback might require host reboot and will impact capacity.
Jordan: Agreed. Also let's collect a small sample of affected drive images for deeper forensic (read-after-write patterns). I'm preparing dd images of the bad sectors.
Isha: Thanks all. I'll post a timeline and incident note in #incidents once RMA ticket is created. If you spot increasing EIO counts, ping here immediately.
